A_target.statement:
Let $G = \struct {V, E}$ be a finite [[Definition:Graph (Graph Theory)|graph]] with [[Definition:Independence Number|independence number]] $\map \alpha G$ and minimum [[Definition:Vertex Cover|vertex cover]] size $\map \tau G$.
Then:
:$\map \alpha G + \map \tau G = \card V$

B_source.statement: A set $S \subseteq V$ is an [[Definition:Independent Set (Graph Theory)|independent set]] {{iff}} $V \setminus S$ is a vertex cover.

derived.complementation: the identity between the two optima

object_map.reformulation: Complementation is an inclusion-reversing bijection taking independent sets to vertex covers, so maximization becomes minimization.

validity_conditions: An edge with both ends in S is exactly an edge missed by V minus S.
The identity makes the two optimization problems polynomially equivalent.
proof_plan: $S \mapsto V \setminus S$ is an inclusion-reversing [[Definition:Bijection|bijection]] on the subsets of $V$.
By the source result, it maps the independent sets onto the vertex covers.
As $\card {V \setminus S} = \card V - \card S$, a maximum independent set corresponds to a minimum vertex cover.
